name: Sign-in, sessions and credentials
summary: How people and machines prove who they are: sign-in methods, access and refresh tokens, session limits, logout, and API keys for integrations.

roles.note: Sign-in applies to every verified user regardless of role. API keys are a separate machine credential, mapped to a project.

actions.action: Sign in and refresh a session
Use an API key on external-capture routes

nfr.statement: How quickly a logout, removal or revoked session stops working across every API (caches included).
nfr.open_question: What maximum revocation delay is acceptable? Today it depends on Redis and downstream caches (T3D-IMPL-123).

requirements.title: Several sign-in methods and password recovery
requirements.statement: Users can sign in with email and password or through one of several external sign-in providers, and can recover a forgotten password. Which providers are offered to which customers is not decided (DEC-011).

acceptance_criteria.given: A verified user who forgot their password
acceptance_criteria.when: They request a password reset and follow the link
acceptance_criteria.then: They can set a new password and sign in with it

requirements.title: Only verified users with a live session reach protected APIs
requirements.statement: Every non-public request needs a valid token belonging to a verified user. If the token is bound to a session, that session must belong to the user and not be revoked.

sources.title: Product walkthrough and clarifications recorded in the 2026-10-28 ledger

open_checks: No production branch was resolved for auth-service and service-kit

acceptance_criteria.given: A signed-in user whose email is not verified
acceptance_criteria.when: They call a protected API through the gateway

acceptance_criteria.given: A token whose session was revoked by logout
acceptance_criteria.when: It is used on a protected API

requirements.title: Access tokens last 15 minutes on web and 24 hours on mobile
requirements.statement: By default an access token lasts 15 minutes for web clients and 24 hours for mobile clients, and environment settings can override both. A client counts as mobile from its user agent (native HTTP clients); browsers and unknown clients count as web.

acceptance_criteria.given: Default settings and a sign-in from a browser
Default settings and a sign-in from the native mobile app

requirements.title: Refreshing never extends a session past its absolute end
requirements.statement: Each session has an absolute end: the earlier of its stored end and its creation time plus the user's allowed session lifetime. A refresh after that point fails, so refreshing can't keep a session alive forever.

acceptance_criteria.given: A session whose absolute end has passed
acceptance_criteria.when: The client presents its refresh token
acceptance_criteria.then: The refresh fails as expired, and the user must sign in again

requirements.title: Refresh tokens rotate, and reuse outside the grace window revokes the session
requirements.statement: Each refresh replaces the refresh token. During a short grace window (30 seconds by default), concurrent refreshes with the previous token get the same new token. Presenting a stale token after the window revokes the whole session.
open_checks: Behaviour on Redis loss and under refresh races is unverified

acceptance_criteria.given: Two tabs refresh with the same token within 30 seconds
acceptance_criteria.then: Both receive the same new refresh token, and the session stays valid

acceptance_criteria.given: A refresh token that was replaced more than 30 seconds ago

requirements.title: Logout ends only the current session
requirements.statement: Logging out revokes the session it was made from. The user's other sessions stay signed in.

acceptance_criteria.given: A user signed in on web and on mobile
acceptance_criteria.then: The web session stops working, and the mobile session keeps working

requirements.title: API keys work only on their mapped project's external-capture routes
requirements.statement: An API key is accepted only on the selected external-capture and folder routes, and only for the project it is mapped to. An API key sent alongside a normal user token on any other route is dropped before the request is forwarded.

acceptance_criteria.given: An API key mapped to project A
acceptance_criteria.when: It is used on an external-capture route for project B
